question: The recorded pair shares no contrast: P-152's 95.8% is AD vs HC, and P-63's 76.88% is CN vs MCI. Both papers, however, report the same three pairwise ADNI staging contrasts (the record's T3), and the MRI channel is shared. P-152 uses diffusion MRI superficial-white-matter features only (24 HC/24 MCI/24 AD, ADNI2). P-63 fuses T1 MRI with SNP and blood miRNA data (158 CN/128 MCI/42 AD) and also reports an MRI-only arm. Following condition 6, the pair is judged on the figures printed for the shared contrasts. On AD vs CN and MCI vs AD the accuracies agree. MCI vs HC is the contrast where a gap exists.

figures.P-152: Internal 5-fold CV, no intervals printed (Table 3). MCI vs HC: accuracy 83.3% (quadratic SVM; 40/48), AUC 0.88. Wilson over 48: 0.704-0.913. Hanley-McNeil for 0.88 with 24/24: Q1 = 0.7857, Q2 = 0.8238, SE = 0.0511, CI 0.780-0.980. Table 3 also prints an undefined 'Correction' column reading 70.3 for MCI-HC. AD vs HC: 95.8%, AUC 0.99 (Wilson 0.860-0.989). MCI vs AD: 83.3% (Wilson 0.704-0.913), AUC 0.93 (Hanley-McNeil CI 0.853-1.000).

matched_figure_check: AD vs CN: 95.8% vs 95.00%, which agree (P-152's AUC 0.99 there is also near-ceiling). MCI vs AD: the accuracies agree (83.3% lies inside both P-63 intervals, and 80.21% and 87.72% lie inside P-152's); the fused AUCs agree. MCI vs HC: P-63 prints the result under P-152's input condition (MRI only), and that matched figure widens the gap rather than closing it. P-152's 83.3% lies outside the MRI-only interval (0.645-0.751). P-63's 70.08% lies just outside P-152's (0.704-0.913), by 0.003. On AUC, 0.88 lies outside 0.708-0.821 and 0.7641 outside 0.780-0.980. Against the record's own P-63 figure (fusion), the accuracy gap holds in one direction only (83.3% outside 0.717-0.814; 76.88% inside P-152's interval), and the AUCs agree (0.88 vs 0.873).
performance_validity: Figure-level: P-152's MCI-vs-HC figures (AUC 0.88, accuracy 83.3%) are below 0.97, and P-63's are too. Study-level: P-152 reports AD vs HC AUC 0.99 on 48 subjects, internal CV only, no external cohort, which meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. The review describes the exclusion as removing such studies from every cross-study comparison. Read that way, P-152 cannot anchor any performance comparison and the pair fails condition 5.

candidate_explanations.quote: After data quality control, 549 ADNI subjects who have complete SNP, GE, and MRI data were retained, where 158 were diagnosed as control normal (CN), 128 were diagnosed as mild cognitive impairment (MCI)

candidate_explanations.difference: The author-named limitation of small sample size.
candidate_explanations.quote: The study limitation is the small sample size of the included subjects.

reason: The ledger's gap (95.8% vs 76.88%) sets AD vs HC against CN vs MCI, a misread. On matched contrasts the accuracies agree for AD vs CN and MCI vs AD. For MCI vs HC, P-152's DTI result (83.3%, AUC 0.88) sits beyond uncertainty from P-63's matched MRI-only arm (70.08%, AUC 0.764) in both directions, marginally on accuracy (z = 2.20 on accuracy, 1.98 on AUC). Against P-63's fused model, the accuracy gap holds in one direction and the AUCs agree. It is borderline rather than yes for three reasons. P-152's own table prints an undefined 'Correction' value of 70.3 for the same contrast, which would agree with P-63. P-152 as a study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its AD-vs-HC contrast. And the qualifying gap lies on a contrast the record did not dispute. If reported, the candidate explanations (DTI vs T1 input, feature selection before CV, per-contrast kernel choice, 48 vs 286 subjects) are not shown to be sufficient.
